column2: How do I link two different documents (same regiment, same family…)?
column3: On a document’s page (📄 Documents tab) or in the viewer: “🔗 Linked documents” → “＋ Link a document…”, choose the document, then the reason (same regiment, same family, same matter, same place, same notary, or another reason you write). The link works both ways; “⋯” changes the reason or removes the link (↶ Undo). Under each link: “In common” (names, places, years, regiments spotted in both transcriptions) and “💡 What this document tells you” (what the other one adds, with its line). In an investigation, “🔗 Links between its documents” shows the pairs, offers “＋ Add to the case file” for a linked document that is missing, and “🔎 Make it a lead”. This is neither the pages of a single document (📑) nor a collection (📚).

column2: How do I make a collection from documents, and search by collection?
column3: 📄 Documents tab (with no document open): “☑ Choose several”, click the documents in page order (a number appears), then “📚 Make a collection with…”: name, reference, place, years, and you arrange the order with ⠿ or ↑ ↓. A multi-page document goes in with all its pages; files that are not images are left out. “📚 Add to a collection…” (also in a document’s “⋯”) adds to the end of an existing collection, without adding again what is already there. The documents stay where they are: the collection groups them. On a document’s page: “📚 In the collection … page 12 of 40”, with the previous and the next page. In the column, “📚 Collections” sorts the documents by collection (each group folds up, “In no collection” too). To search: the collection’s name in “Search…”, or “Filter ▾” → Collection, Record type (only births…), Town or place and “Within a radius of (km)”, years. The radius needs the place’s coordinates (Places).

column2: How do I see where a collection stands (transcribed, checked, absent pages)?
column3: Lists → 📚 Collections → a collection → “🗂 Status” tab: one box per page, one colour per status (⚪ To do, 🟡 In progress, 🔵 Checked, 🟢 Finished — the same as in the Workshop), the figures, the reliability (deduced from checked lines and “[?]”), and “📋 What’s left, in the recommended order”. The status is calculated automatically (the Workshop record on the photo, or a written text); on the page, you can choose it by hand (↺ back to the calculation), note the legibility and “📷 Photo to retake”. An absent page has a reason (missing, lost, not photographed, not digitised, not online, not open to the public, being restored, elsewhere, blank page) and can join the Archive gaps; “📮 Add to requests” puts it in Research → Register tracking → Requests. Enter the numbering (paginated, foliated, no order for a bundle) and the number of expected pages: the app flags gaps (“after f° 15 v° comes f° 18 r°”) and offers to add the absent pages. “☑ Choose pages” changes several pages at once; “⤓ Export the status” gives a spreadsheet. Everything can be undone (↶ Undo).
